description: Circular conducting loop in decreasing applied magnetic flux. Five external B traces, the hatched loop and both small solid/broken source-visual details are retained. Small details are deliberately unlabelled and carry no asserted current or local-field identity. Both printed B-prime labels are retained by disclosed modern text-binding relocation with leaders to the known axial induced-field annotation, aligned with B under the lesson's positive convention. Affected author candidate; independent review pending.

authoritativeText.text:
ZH: 电磁感应定律
现在来定量描述**电磁感应定律**。
法拉第的实验表明，导体回路中的感生电流强度$I_i$，与穿过回路面积的磁场$\vec{B}$的磁力线数目变化的快慢成正比。
用**磁通量**$\Phi$，可以更准确地表述这个结果。

**磁通量**表示磁场穿过面积$S$的多少，可以用穿过这个面积的磁力线数目来形象表示。
磁力线数目变化的快慢，对应磁通量的变化率。

如果磁通量在很短的时间$\Delta t$内改变了$\Delta\Phi$，它的变化率就是$\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}$。
因此，实验结果可以写成：

**感生电流强度与穿过回路面积的磁通量变化率成正比：**

$I_i\propto\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}$。
(12-3)

当非静电力，也就是这里所说的外来力，作用于导体中的自由电荷时，回路中会出现电流。
单位正电荷沿闭合回路运动时，这些力所做的功叫做**电动势**。

穿过回路面积的磁通量发生变化时，回路中也会出现这种作用。
描述这一作用的电动势叫做**感生电动势**，记作$\mathcal{E}_i$。

根据全电路欧姆定律，$I_i=\frac{\mathcal{E}_i}{R}$。
在这里，导体回路的电阻不随磁通量的变化而改变。
因此，关系式 (12-3) 成立，是因为感生电动势与$\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}$成正比。

**电磁感应定律描述的是电动势，而不是电流强度**。
这样，定律就不依赖产生感生电流的导体本身的性质。
它指出：**闭合回路中感生电动势的大小，等于穿过回路面积的磁通量变化率的绝对值**①：

① 实验直接确定的，只是$\mathcal{E}_i$与$\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}$成正比。
如果磁通量的单位还没有规定，就可以选择这个单位，使比例系数等于1.

$|\mathcal{E}_i|=\left|\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}\right|$。

怎样把**楞次定律**给出的感生电流方向，或者感生电动势的正负号，写进电磁感应定律呢？

图 286 画出了一个圆形回路。
我们作如下正方向约定：如果回路内部由感生电流产生的磁场$\vec{B}'$，与引起感应的磁场$\vec{B}$方向一致，就把电流和电动势记为**正**。

根据楞次定律，磁场$\vec{B}'$和$\vec{B}$同向，是因为引起感应的磁通量正在减少，即$\Delta\Phi<0$，所以$\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}<0$。
要让这时的感生电动势按约定取正，就必须在电磁感应定律中加入一个**负号**：

图 286

$\mathcal{E}_i=-\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}$。
(12-4)

inventory.description: Source pixels: one upright perspective oval for the circular loop, with diagonal hatching and heavier left edge. Modern addition: a regular polygon approximation, sparse hatch density and neutral area fill; hatch count is not source data.

Source trace1, of five: traverses the loop left-to-right, with an outgoing rightward arrow. Upper/lower traces bend away vertically; the middle trace is axial. Modern regularization: smooth sampled curve, not a measured field map.

Source trace2, of five: traverses the loop left-to-right, with an outgoing rightward arrow. Upper/lower traces bend away vertically; the middle trace is axial. Modern regularization: smooth sampled curve, not a measured field map.

Source trace3, of five: traverses the loop left-to-right, with an outgoing rightward arrow. Upper/lower traces bend away vertically; the middle trace is axial. Modern regularization: smooth sampled curve, not a measured field map.

Source trace4, of five: traverses the loop left-to-right, with an outgoing rightward arrow. Upper/lower traces bend away vertically; the middle trace is axial. Modern regularization: smooth sampled curve, not a measured field map.

Source trace5, of five: traverses the loop left-to-right, with an outgoing rightward arrow. Upper/lower traces bend away vertically; the middle trace is axial. Modern regularization: smooth sampled curve, not a measured field map.

Source pixels: B at top-right; two printed B-prime labels beside the lower-left broken small return and above the right small detail. Modern text-binding relocation, NOT source-pixel placement: retain both printed B-prime symbols as source-left-B-prime-label and source-right-B-prime-label in the modern axial-field annotation band; visible leader segments terminate on text-induced-field-direction. All three B-prime labels there denote the same induced field defined inside the loop by the lesson, not the small visual details or any of the five external B traces. The two relocated labels are retained printed symbols, not two extra physical fields.

Source pixels only: small left closed-outline solid-upper/broken-lower visual detail beside/crossing the loop rim. The upper short arrow runs rightward and visibly rises; the lower return has broken strokes and no added arrowhead. Retained UNLABELLED structural detail, with no asserted current or local-field identity. Stable historical IDs containing 'circulation' name source strokes only, not physical semantics. The adjacent printed B-prime label is separately accounted for by the disclosed source-labels relocation to the known modern axial induced-field annotation. Endpoint and slope assertions certify visual relationships only.

Source pixels only: small right closed-outline solid-upper/broken-lower visual detail beside/crossing the loop rim. The upper short arrow runs rightward and descends; the lower return has broken strokes and no added arrowhead. Retained UNLABELLED structural detail, with no asserted current or local-field identity. Stable historical IDs containing 'circulation' name source strokes only, not physical semantics. The adjacent printed B-prime label is separately accounted for by the disclosed source-labels relocation to the known modern axial induced-field annotation. Endpoint and slope assertions certify visual relationships only.

Justified modern text-binding addition, not a source pixel object: a direction arrow for the field inside the loop. The paired arrows both point right, exactly matching the positive convention in the whole edition text.

Justified modern text-binding annotation, not source pixels: B-prime produced by induced current is the field inside the loop, aligned and same-direction with inducing B under the stated positive convention. This axial-direction annotation remains unchanged. The two printed B-prime symbols are retained separately with leaders in source-labels; they share this known referent. Neither this assertion nor the relocated labels assign a field/current identity to either small solid/broken visual detail.
Modern text-binding captions identify decreasing flux and the positive-current/EMF case. They are not claims of additional source-image words or an increasing-flux subfigure.
